rules.statement: The undertaking shall assess sustainability matters under both impact materiality and financial materiality (double materiality), reporting any matter that is material from either perspective or both.

Impact materiality concerns the undertaking's actual or potential, positive or negative impacts on people and the environment over the short, medium and long term, including impacts connected with its own operations and value chain.

A sustainability matter is financially material when it triggers or could reasonably be expected to trigger material financial effects on the undertaking's development, performance, position, cost of capital or access to finance in the short, medium or long term.
The sustainability statement shall cover the undertaking's own operations and, to the extent of material impacts, risks and opportunities, its upstream and downstream value chain.
The undertaking shall apply the defined reporting time horizons: short-term (the reporting period), medium-term (up to five years after the reporting period) and long-term (beyond five years).

The sustainability statement shall be presented in a clearly identifiable section of the management report and structured around governance, strategy, impact/risk/opportunity management, and metrics and targets.
The undertaking shall disclose comparative information in respect of the previous period for all quantitative metrics and monetary amounts reported.
The undertaking shall disclose the general basis for preparation of its sustainability statement, including the scope of consolidation and whether value-chain information is included.

The undertaking shall disclose specific circumstances affecting preparation, including use of time horizons, value-chain estimation, sources of estimation uncertainty, and changes in preparation or presentation.
The undertaking shall disclose the composition and diversity of the administrative, management and supervisory bodies and their roles and responsibilities regarding sustainability matters.
The undertaking shall disclose how the administrative, management and supervisory bodies are informed about material sustainability impacts, risks and opportunities and how those were addressed.
The undertaking shall disclose whether and how sustainability-related performance is integrated into incentive schemes for members of the administrative, management and supervisory bodies.
The undertaking shall disclose a mapping of how the core elements of the due-diligence process are covered in the sustainability statement.
The undertaking shall disclose the main features of its risk management and internal control system in relation to the sustainability reporting process.
The undertaking shall disclose its strategy, business model and value chain, including significant groups of products/services, markets and the sustainability-related elements of its strategy.
The undertaking shall disclose the interests and views of its stakeholders and how they are taken into account in the strategy and business model.
The undertaking shall disclose its material impacts, risks and opportunities and their interaction with its strategy and business model.
The undertaking shall disclose the process used to identify and assess material impacts, risks and opportunities, including the methodologies and assumptions applied.
The undertaking shall disclose which ESRS disclosure requirements are covered by its statement and provide a list of the datapoints reported or omitted on materiality grounds.
For each material sustainability matter, the undertaking shall disclose the policies adopted to manage it, including scope, accountability and reference to third-party standards.
For each material sustainability matter, the undertaking shall disclose the actions and resources allocated to address it, including expected outcomes and time horizons.
For each material sustainability matter, the undertaking shall disclose measurable, outcome-oriented targets, their baselines, the period to which they relate and progress against them.
The undertaking shall disclose its transition plan for climate change mitigation, including its compatibility with limiting global warming to 1.5 °C in line with the Paris Agreement.
The undertaking shall disclose the material physical and transition climate-related risks and opportunities identified, including the resilience of its strategy and business model.

The undertaking shall describe the process to identify and assess material climate-related impacts, risks and opportunities, including the climate scenarios used for physical and transition risk screening.
The undertaking shall disclose its policies for climate change mitigation and adaptation.
The undertaking shall disclose its climate mitigation and adaptation actions and the financial and other resources allocated, including current and future CapEx/OpEx aligned with the transition plan.
The undertaking shall disclose its GHG emission reduction targets in absolute value (and where relevant intensity), with base year, target years and whether they are science-based.
The undertaking shall disclose total energy consumption in MWh disaggregated by fossil, nuclear and renewable sources, and the share of renewable energy in total consumption.
Undertakings in high climate-impact sectors shall disclose their energy intensity (total energy consumption per net revenue) associated with activities in those sectors.
The undertaking shall disclose its gross Scope 1 GHG emissions in metric tonnes of CO2-equivalent, and the percentage covered by regulated emission trading schemes.
The undertaking shall disclose its gross Scope 2 GHG emissions in metric tonnes of CO2-equivalent, reported both location-based and market-based.
The undertaking shall disclose its gross Scope 3 GHG emissions in metric tonnes of CO2-equivalent, broken down by significant value-chain categories of the GHG Protocol.
The undertaking shall disclose total GHG emissions as the sum of Scope 1, 2 and 3, and the GHG intensity per net revenue.
The undertaking shall disclose GHG removals and storage in its own operations and value chain, and the amount of carbon credits cancelled or planned to be cancelled, in tonnes of CO2-equivalent.
The undertaking shall disclose whether it applies internal carbon pricing schemes, the type and scope of schemes, the prices applied, and how they support decision-making.
The undertaking shall disclose the anticipated financial effects from material physical and transition risks and from climate-related opportunities, including assets and net revenue at risk.
Where relevant, the undertaking shall reconcile climate-related CapEx and OpEx in its transition plan with the EU Taxonomy CapEx and OpEx plans disclosed under the Taxonomy Regulation.
The undertaking shall disclose its policies for managing material impacts, risks and opportunities related to pollution prevention and control.
The undertaking shall disclose the actions and resources taken to prevent, mitigate or remediate pollution of air, water and soil.
The undertaking shall disclose the measurable targets it has set in relation to pollution prevention and control.
The undertaking shall disclose the amounts of pollutants emitted to air, water and soil, including those listed in the E-PRTR Regulation, in the relevant units of mass.
The undertaking shall disclose the quantities of substances of concern and substances of very high concern that it generates or uses in production, or that leave its facilities.
The undertaking shall disclose the anticipated financial effects from material pollution-related risks and opportunities.
The undertaking shall disclose its policies for managing material impacts, risks and opportunities related to water and marine resources.
The undertaking shall disclose actions and resources taken to manage water and marine resources, including in areas at water risk.
The undertaking shall disclose the measurable targets it has set for water and marine resources.
The undertaking shall disclose total water consumption in cubic metres, the share in areas at water risk, and water intensity per net revenue.
The undertaking shall disclose the anticipated financial effects from material water and marine resource-related risks and opportunities.
The undertaking shall disclose how its biodiversity and ecosystems strategy and business model are resilient and compatible with relevant biodiversity transition objectives.
The undertaking shall disclose its policies for managing material impacts, dependencies, risks and opportunities related to biodiversity and ecosystems.
The undertaking shall disclose actions and resources related to biodiversity and ecosystems, referencing the mitigation hierarchy of avoid, minimise, restore and offset.
The undertaking shall disclose the measurable targets it has set in relation to biodiversity and ecosystems.

The undertaking shall disclose metrics on impacts on biodiversity and ecosystems, including land-use change, the area of sites near biodiversity-sensitive areas, and species/ecosystem condition metrics.
The undertaking shall disclose the anticipated financial effects from material biodiversity and ecosystem-related risks and opportunities.
The undertaking shall disclose its policies for managing material impacts, risks and opportunities related to resource use and the circular economy.
The undertaking shall disclose actions and resources to increase resource efficiency, transition to circular practices and reduce waste.
The undertaking shall disclose the measurable targets it has set for resource use and the circular economy.
The undertaking shall disclose resource inflows, including the overall total weight of products and materials used and the share of biological and secondary (recycled) materials.
The undertaking shall disclose resource outflows including total waste generated in tonnes, the share diverted from disposal and the share directed to disposal, by treatment type.
The undertaking shall disclose the anticipated financial effects from material resource-use and circular-economy risks and opportunities.
The undertaking shall disclose the material impacts, risks and opportunities relating to its own workforce and how they affect its strategy and business model.
The undertaking shall disclose its policies for managing material impacts, risks and opportunities related to its own workforce, including respect for human rights.
The undertaking shall describe the processes to remediate negative impacts and the channels available for its own workforce to raise concerns.
The undertaking shall disclose the total number of employees by head count or full-time equivalent, broken down by gender and by country where it has significant employment.
The undertaking shall disclose the total number of non-employees in its own workforce (self-employed people and workers provided by employment agencies).
The undertaking shall disclose the percentage of employees covered by collective bargaining agreements and the extent of employee representation in social dialogue.
The undertaking shall disclose gender distribution at top management level and the distribution of employees by age group.

The undertaking shall disclose health and safety metrics, including the percentage of own workforce covered by its health and safety system, the number and rate of recordable work-related accidents, and work-related fatalities.

The undertaking shall disclose the gender pay gap (difference in average pay between female and male employees) and the ratio of the annual total remuneration of the highest-paid individual to the median annual total remuneration.
The undertaking shall disclose the number of work-related incidents of discrimination, complaints and severe human-rights incidents, and the related fines, penalties and compensation.
The undertaking shall disclose its policies for managing material impacts, risks and opportunities related to workers in its value chain.
The undertaking shall disclose its processes for engaging with value-chain workers and their representatives about actual and potential impacts.
The undertaking shall describe the processes to remediate negative impacts and the channels available for value-chain workers to raise concerns.
The undertaking shall disclose actions taken on material impacts on value-chain workers, approaches to manage material risks and pursue opportunities, and the effectiveness of those actions.
The undertaking shall disclose the time-bound and outcome-oriented targets it has set in relation to value-chain workers.
The undertaking shall disclose its policies for managing material impacts, risks and opportunities related to affected communities.
The undertaking shall disclose its processes for engaging with affected communities about actual and potential impacts.
The undertaking shall describe the processes to remediate negative impacts and the channels available for affected communities to raise concerns.
The undertaking shall disclose actions taken on material impacts on affected communities and the effectiveness of those actions.
The undertaking shall disclose the time-bound and outcome-oriented targets it has set in relation to affected communities.
The undertaking shall disclose its policies for managing material impacts, risks and opportunities related to consumers and end-users.
The undertaking shall disclose its processes for engaging with consumers and end-users about actual and potential impacts.
The undertaking shall describe the processes to remediate negative impacts and the channels available for consumers and end-users to raise concerns.
The undertaking shall disclose actions taken on material impacts on consumers and end-users and the effectiveness of those actions.
The undertaking shall disclose the time-bound and outcome-oriented targets it has set in relation to consumers and end-users.
The undertaking shall disclose the role of the administrative, management and supervisory bodies related to business conduct, including their expertise on business-conduct matters.

The undertaking shall disclose its policies on corporate culture and business conduct, including mechanisms to identify, report and investigate concerns about unlawful behaviour and protection of whistleblowers.
The undertaking shall disclose its approach to managing relationships with suppliers and its policies to prevent late payments, especially towards SMEs.
The undertaking shall disclose its systems to prevent and detect corruption and bribery, including the related training provided.
The undertaking shall disclose the number of confirmed incidents of corruption or bribery, the number of convictions and the amount of fines for violation of anti-corruption and anti-bribery laws.
The undertaking shall disclose its activities and commitments related to exercising political influence, including financial and in-kind political contributions and lobbying.
The undertaking shall disclose its payment practices, including the average time to pay invoices, the standard payment terms, and the number of legal proceedings for late payments.

An entity shall disclose information about sustainability-related risks and opportunities that could reasonably be expected to affect its cash flows, access to finance or cost of capital over the short, medium or long term.
An entity shall disclose the governance processes, controls and procedures it uses to monitor, manage and oversee sustainability-related risks and opportunities.

An entity shall disclose its strategy for managing sustainability-related risks and opportunities, including effects on its business model, value chain and financial position, performance and cash flows.
An entity shall disclose the processes it uses to identify, assess, prioritise and monitor sustainability-related risks and opportunities and how they are integrated into overall risk management.
An entity shall disclose metrics and targets used to measure and monitor its performance in relation to material sustainability-related risks and opportunities, including progress against targets.
Information is material if omitting, misstating or obscuring it could reasonably be expected to influence decisions of primary users of general purpose financial reports.

Sustainability-related financial disclosures shall be connected to and reported for the same reporting period as the related financial statements, enabling users to assess the links between information.
An entity shall provide sustainability-related disclosures as part of its general purpose financial reports and at the same time as the related financial statements.
An entity shall disclose comparative information in respect of the preceding period for all amounts reported in the current period, and revise comparatives when estimates change.
An entity shall disclose the governance body or individual responsible for oversight of climate-related risks and opportunities, and management's role and controls in monitoring them.

An entity shall disclose the climate-related risks and opportunities that could reasonably be expected to affect its prospects, classifying each risk as a physical or transition risk and specifying the time horizon.
An entity shall disclose the current and anticipated effects of climate-related risks and opportunities on its business model and value chain.
An entity shall disclose the effects of climate-related risks and opportunities on its strategy and decision-making, including any climate-related transition plan and targets.

An entity shall disclose the current and anticipated effects of climate-related risks and opportunities on its financial position, financial performance and cash flows over the short, medium and long term.
An entity shall disclose its assessment of climate resilience using climate-related scenario analysis, including the inputs, key assumptions and the analytical choices it made.
An entity shall disclose the processes it uses to identify, assess, prioritise and monitor climate-related risks and opportunities and how they are integrated into overall risk management.
An entity shall disclose its absolute gross Scope 1 greenhouse gas emissions in metric tonnes of CO2-equivalent, measured in accordance with the Greenhouse Gas Protocol Corporate Standard.
An entity shall disclose its absolute gross Scope 2 greenhouse gas emissions in metric tonnes of CO2-equivalent, using a location-based measurement and information about contractual instruments.
An entity shall disclose its absolute gross Scope 3 greenhouse gas emissions in metric tonnes of CO2-equivalent, including the categories of the GHG Protocol included in the measure.
An entity with asset-management, commercial-banking or insurance activities shall disclose its financed emissions (additional Scope 3 information) in accordance with the industry-based requirements.
An entity shall disclose the amount and percentage of assets or business activities vulnerable to climate-related transition risks.
An entity shall disclose the amount and percentage of assets or business activities vulnerable to climate-related physical risks.
An entity shall disclose the amount and percentage of assets or business activities aligned with climate-related opportunities.
An entity shall disclose the amount of capital expenditure, financing or investment deployed towards climate-related risks and opportunities.
An entity that applies a carbon price in decision-making shall disclose the price for each metric tonne of GHG emissions and explain how it is applied.
An entity shall disclose the percentage of executive management remuneration recognised in the current period that is linked to climate-related considerations.
An entity shall disclose industry-based metrics associated with its business model and activities, referring to the Industry-based Guidance on Implementing IFRS S2.

An entity shall disclose each quantitative and qualitative climate-related target, including the metric, objective, base period, milestones, whether it is absolute or intensity-based, and how it compares with the latest international agreement on climate change.

An entity shall measure its greenhouse gas emissions in accordance with the Greenhouse Gas Protocol Corporate Standard (2004) unless required by a jurisdictional authority or exchange to use a different method.
